title: Magnetoresistance in Magnetic Weyl semimetal Mn$_{3}$ZnC
abstract: The magnetoresistance (MR) in magnetic materials reveal an intriguing spin-dependent electron scattering, highlighting the role of spin polarization on the electronic transport properties. This becomes even more interesting for the topological magnetic materials where a finite Berry curvature leads to an intrinsic scattering channel also. In this report, we investigate MR of Mn$_{3}$ZnC, an antiperovskite magnetic nodal line semimetal. Mn$_{3}$ZnC shows a ferromagnetic (FM) transition at $\sim$ 420 K, followed by an ferrimagnetic (FIM) transition at $\sim$ 195 K. We focus on the interpretation of MR data and highlight the relation between MR and its magnetization. The signature of magnetization induced MR shows correlation at low magnetic fields and displays distinct behaviors in the FIM and FM states. Similar to the isothermal magnetization M(H) curve of FM and FIM state, the MR curves exhibit a sharp increase, followed by a linear behavior at higher fields. As the magnetic field varies, the cusp-like anomaly becomes more pronounced, and vanishes at the magnetic phase transition, which then reappears as the temperature increases. The sign change in the MR curves in the FIM state is attributed to a drastic change in the carrier mobility. Interestingly, this system shows a positive MR in FM state at very low field, which is quite unusual.
summary: This paper reports on magnetoresistance measurements in the magnetic nodal line semimetal Mn3ZnC, demonstrating a clear link between MR anomalies and the material's ferromagnetic/ferrimagnetic transitions. By analyzing how MR changes with field and temperature relative to magnetization, the authors suggest that quantum transport effects related to spin-dependent scattering govern the electronic behavior.
main_problem: The study investigates magnetoresistance (MR) in magnetic topological semimetals to understand how spin-dependent electron scattering mechanisms couple with magnetic ordering.
main_result: The MR behavior is strongly correlated with the material's magnetic state (FM vs. FIM), showing distinct field and temperature dependencies that suggest quantum transport effects dominate over classical models.
method: The research combines experimental measurements of MR versus applied magnetic field and temperature with theoretical analysis comparing observed power laws to established quantum transport theories.
model_or_system: The system under study is Mn3ZnC, an antiperovskite nodal line semimetal exhibiting both ferromagnetic (FM) and ferrimagnetic (FIM) transitions. The analysis draws parallels with general topological magnetic materials.
key_observables: Magnetoresistance (MR), magnetization ($M$), carrier mobility ($\mu$), and the field/temperature dependence of MR power laws ($	ext{MR} \propto H^p$ or $	ext{MR} \propto M^ eta$).
important_parameters: Magnetic transition temperatures ($\sim 420	ext{ K}$ FM, $\sim 195	ext{ K}$ FIM), low-field critical fields ($B^*$), and high magnetic field regimes ($\geq 2	ext{ T}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis tests applicability of various transport models (PL model, Guiding Center Diffusion) and ultimately favors quantum limit theories due to low sample mobility.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate MR vs. H at varying T across magnetic transitions; contour plots show low-field MR dependence on field/temperature; magnetization curves track the FM/FIM states.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes MR data, first establishing the correlation between MR and $M(H)$ in different magnetic phases (FM vs. FIM). It then compares observed field dependencies to theoretical models before concluding with interpretations based on quantum transport limits.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the strong dependence of electronic transport properties (MR) on spin polarization and topological band structure provides insights into emergent quantum phenomena relevant to correlated electron systems.
